Instrument.name: Radio Science Subsystem for GO
Instrument.description: The Galileo Radio Science investigations combined instruments on the spacecraft and the Deep Space Network (DSN) for telecommunications and radio science. Two teams conducted experiments: the Celestial Mechanics Team, focusing on general relativity and gravitational models of Jupiter, and the Radio Propagation Team, studying solar and Jovian atmospheres. The spacecraft used a telecommunications subsystem with various frequencies and operational modes, but issues with the high-gain antenna hampered data collection. Key scientific objectives included gravity measurements, General Relativity tests, and solar corona observations, contributing to our understanding of Jupiter, its satellites, and gravitational phenomena. The DSN tracked the spacecraft and managed data collection, playing a vital role in the success of these investigations.
